outcome_evidence: Command: `echo hello` (cwd /workspace) -> exit code 125, output: 'Cannot connect to Podman... Error: unable to connect to Podman socket: failed to connect: ssh: handshake failed: read tcp 127.0.0.1:56484->127.0.0.1:59571: wsarecv: An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host.'
Command: `true` (cwd /workspace) -> exit code 125, same Podman/SSH handshake failure; no command output produced
Command: `cd /workspace && ls -la` -> exit code 125, same Podman/SSH handshake failure; directory listing not obtained
Command: `whoami && hostname` -> exit code 125, same Podman/SSH handshake failure
Command: `sleep 300 && echo alive` (delayed retry) -> exit code 125, same Podman/SSH handshake failure, confirming the outage is persistent and not transient
Approximately 20 terminal invocations across several minutes of inter-command waits all failed identically before any command could execute; no files, processes, ports or services could be inspected
assessment_summary: Goal: independently validate that the URBO installation (documented `just up` workflow) is complete and operational. Method: I attempted to inspect the container filesystem, installed tooling (just/node/pnpm/docker/java), Docker containers, and instance state (`.urbo-instance`, `/workspace/.urbo/urbo/`), then to run runtime checks (`just doctor`, `just status`, `docker ps`, HTTP probes to the `*.urbo.localhost` URLs). Result: none of these could be executed. Every terminal call — including trivial commands like `echo hello` and `true` — failed before execution with exit code 125 and the error `Cannot connect to Podman ... ssh: handshake failed ... An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host`, originating from the agent's own shell transport (the tool is proxied through a Podman/SSH socket), not from URBO. I retried roughly 20 times, including waits of 15s–300s, and the failure was 100% consistent, demonstrating a persistent infrastructure outage rather than a transient glitch. Because no command ever returned real output, I obtained no objective evidence about the installation: I could neither confirm components (containers, backend API, MeiliSearch, Keycloak, proxy, dev servers, seeded data) are healthy/operational, nor show that anything is missing or broken. The supplied installation summary independently corroborates this, stating the sandbox shell backend became permanently unreachable (repeated Podman/SSH handshake errors) about an hour after startup. Limitations: the validation harness/container transport is down, so inspection, startup, and interface queries were all impossible; the summary's claims (healthy `spring-app`, `keycloak`, `localstack`, `postgres`, `meilisearch`, `imgproxy`, `sample-images`, shared `urbo-proxy`, 200 responses from `/v3/api-docs`, MeiliSearch `available`, completed sample-data seed, dummy-token build success) remain unverified by me. Uncertainty: since no behavior could be observed, neither success nor failure can be established. For these reasons the assessed outcome is `inconclusive`, pending restoration of the shell backend and re-validation.
